title: AdminContext
description: The context EVERY administrative command carries, derived from identity_application::administration::AdminContext. The second field is not redundancy: the session is what proves the actor at AAL2, and a destructive administrative action that did not check the actor's assurance level would be reachable from a session the actor merely LOGGED INTO.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; no administrative command has a body

actor_id.description: The administrator acting. Whose session it is comes from the Admin Worker's own session; it is never taken from the request body at the Identity Worker, because a body field is the caller asserting who they are.
actor_id.x-derivation: re-derived by the Identity Worker from the session, not read from the body — see docs/architecture/overview.md, where the Admin Worker 're-derives the actor' before the rule is evaluated

actor_session_id.description: The session the administrator is acting under. Checked for AAL2 on every command that changes someone else's security posture. This is the field the AAL2 check has to happen against: without it there is nowhere to check.
actor_session_id.x-test: identity_application::administration::tests::every_administrative_command_carries_a_session asserts context.actor_session_id is present on SuspendUser, UnsuspendUser, RevokeUserSessions and ChangeUserRole

x-aal2-requirement.rule: every command that changes someone else's security posture requires the actor's session to be at AAL2
x-aal2-requirement.refusal: identity_application::administration::forbidden_reason_missing_aal2 — ONE named function rather than an inline string at each call site, so the audit of authorization failures has a single reason to group by
x-aal2-requirement.reason_text: administrative action requires an AAL2 session
x-aal2-requirement.not-on-the-wire: the refusal is an ApplicationError::Forbidden and reaches a client as code 'forbidden' (403). The reason string is for the audit trail.
